subject: SIG follow-up — data preservation, prompt logs & training opt-out (Meditex)

Subject: SIG: questions on prompt/log retention + training opt-out

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the SIG. We've started to map Redwood's answers into our internal risk tracker and have a couple of follow-ups specifically around data handling we hope you can clarify quickly:

1) Prompt/log retention: please confirm default retention windows for prompt text and full request/response logs (both ephemeral cache and persisted logs). Do you retain full-text anywhere beyond the default window for debugging or billing?

2) Training on customer content: does Redwood use customer prompts or responses to improve models (training or finetuning) by default? If not, what's the opt-in process and how is that captured in contracts?

3) KV cache / prefix caching: does persistent caching retain customer data beyond the scope of the request? Any details on encryption-at-rest and retention are helpful.

4) Evidence: can you attach a short policy excerpt and any signed attestation for training opt-out we can stash in the GRC folder? Also, if you can supply an architecture diagram for caching that would help our reviewers.

I've attached the SIG template (Meditex_SIG_Response_Template.xlsx) — if it's easier we can take your doc and copy into the template. Looking to close this section by end of week.

Can we get a response today or tomorrow? Happy to hop on a 15-min call if it helps.

Thanks,

Team — forwarding Ben's follow-up from Meditex. Ben needs concise answers plus three artifacts: policy excerpt, training-optout attestation, and a KV cache diagram.

Draft answers I propose (short bullets we can paste into the template):
- Prompt & request/response logs: short-term ephemeral logs for request throughput/seq processing are held only in-memory and flushed; persisted operational logs (for billing, debugging, and abuse investigation) are retained by default for 90 days and then purged.
- Training on customer content: Redwood does NOT train models on customer data by default. Training/finetuning on customer data occurs only under explicit, written agreement; opt-in is contractually captured via an addendum and logged in our training consent registry.
- KV cache: KV cache is per-request/prefix ephemeral, not stored as customer-identifiable artifacts beyond the request lifetime; any persisted cache snapshots used for performance analytics are anonymized and aggregated.

Dev/Soojin — can you: 1) confirm the retention windows and exact language for the policy excerpt; 2) attach the signed attestation we keep for training opt-out; 3) export the KV cache architecture diagram (PNG/PDF).

Ben — I'll assemble and send you a single packet once I have artifacts.

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the items you requested and the short-form answers you can paste into the SIG template. If you prefer, we can also drop these into your XLS and return.

Quick answers (paste-ready):
- Prompt & request/response logs: Redwood maintains ephemeral in-memory request state (including KV cache and transient prompt material) that is not persisted after request completion. Operational request logs (used for billing, debugging, and incident analysis) are persisted by default for 90 days and are then purged; customers may request shorter retention via contract or config. We do not retain full-text prompts beyond operational retention for the purposes of model training or continuous improvement unless a customer explicitly opts in.

- Training on customer content: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or responses to train or fine-tune models by default. Any model training that incorporates customer data requires an explicit, auditable opt-in (contract addendum and signed attestation). Customers who opt-in are assigned an internal tracking id and the scope and timeframe are recorded in our training consent registry.

- KV cache / prefix caching: The KV cache is a per-request/per-session mechanism to accelerate in-flight decoding and is not persisted as a customer-facing dataset. Durable caching is disabled by default for customer data. Any telemetry-derived performance snapshots are anonymized and aggregated; encryption-at-rest is enabled for persisted operational logs and snapshots.

Attachments included: redwood_prompt_log_policy_v2.pdf (policy excerpt, highlights retention language), redwood_training_optout_attestation.pdf (signed attestation template we issue to customers), redwood_kvcache_arch.pdf (diagram and short notes). We also included a short pointer to our SOC 2 report on the GRC Drive.
